a.attack: A monthly list with three parallel tasks gains a mode selector before the user can identify the actual elapsed estimate; this adds another decision rather than reducing clutter.
a.response: Suggested repair: show the elapsed estimate by default and expose ordinary/parallel presentation only inside its breakdown, with unchanged calculations and settings.
a.scoreReason: Preserves settings well, but a new presentation mode consumes attention and has weaker guidance for narrow layouts.

b.attack: A 320px shopping row with date, duration and price cannot maintain readable aligned columns and 44px field targets simultaneously.
b.response: Suggested repair: retain identity and essential context on the first line; stack named field actions in the existing supplemental disclosure when columns no longer fit.
b.scoreReason: A flat ledger reduces ornamental competition while retaining direct field routes; responsive disclosure is concrete, although field prioritization needs care.

revisedWinner.mechanism: Retain the flat ledger and single glass toolbar; align named totals only where they fit, and stack supplemental field actions in an expandable line when width is constrained.
revisedWinner.visible: Identity, completion, exact reference period, inclusion scope and relevant deadline; applicable labeled totals where readable.
revisedWinner.disclosed: Supplemental task fields expose every original editor and link; toolbar and section controls retain scope, diagnostic, breakdown and unchanged menus.
revisedWinner.access: Semantic 44px field controls, stable keyboard order, scoped names and visible focus; no horizontal ledger scrolling at 320px, with reduced motion.

a.attack: Two identically named nested sections with flattened context rows can make their duration and inclusion controls appear to belong to the same parent.
a.response: Suggested repair: retain hierarchy guides and name each context control using its complete ancestor path; keep the row adjacent to its own section heading.
a.scoreReason: Directly addresses nested mobile width while preserving local action scope; explicit ancestor descriptions make the tradeoff manageable.

b.attack: Opening an inspector beside a five-level list shrinks already constrained task rows; an unrelated selected object can remain displayed while the user acts elsewhere.
b.response: Suggested repair: use a sheet whenever remaining content width is inadequate, visibly identify the inspected object, and restore focus safely after deletion.
b.scoreReason: Strong focus semantics but adds selection state, panel management and width pressure for a problem already local to each row.

revisedWinner.mechanism: Keep hierarchy guides but place local context and Details outside deep indentation; bind each full-width context row to its adjacent heading and complete ancestor path.
revisedWinner.visible: Hierarchy cue, local context, title/count, completion and exact global period/inclusion scope.
revisedWinner.disclosed: Context exposes period, duration and inclusion; separate Options retains the original section menu; task Details preserves all editors and links.
revisedWinner.access: 44px nonoverlapping controls, full ancestor labels, independent collapse and disclosure, visible keyboard focus and wrapping at 320px.

a.attack: A current-month title with a rolled-over section can imply that the section completion belongs to the visible month unless its exception remains explicit.
a.response: Suggested repair: keep the exact selected period and local exception beside section identity, and expose the existing navigator through a clearly labeled Periodo button.
a.scoreReason: Good temporal orientation, but repeating contextual descriptions adds height and the mechanism primarily resolves dates rather than overall metadata clutter.

b.attack: Opening every properties shelf in a virtualized nested list may create overlapping rows if expansion is not measured independently of section collapse.
b.response: Suggested repair: remeasure each expanded row and keep separate buttons for collapse, local scope and metadata, with scope words still visible when closed.
b.scoreReason: Offers predictable homes for each type of information with explicit closed-state scope and independent controls; expansion height is testable.

revisedWinner.mechanism: Use independent Resumen, Alcance and Propiedades shelves at their relevant object level; preserve scope words and real local overrides beside closed summaries, with measured expansion.
revisedWinner.visible: Exact period, active inclusion, local overrides, titles, completion and named shelf controls.
revisedWinner.disclosed: Resumen retains diagnostic and duration routes; Alcance retains inclusion and breakdown; task Propiedades retains all metadata actions and links without duplicating menus.
revisedWinner.access: 44px semantic shelf controls, independent section collapse, stable focus and measured virtualized heights; no hover-only access or horizontal overflow.

a.attack: A frequency map spanning twenty nested sections can become a second navigation hierarchy that users must search just to change one section's inclusion.
a.response: Suggested repair: bound map height, show complete paths, and retain a direct local scope control so the map remains optional composition inspection.
a.scoreReason: Preserves composition information, but adds a large aggregate surface and greater route complexity than a local contextual solution.

b.attack: A weekly block caption may hide a task's independently configured monthly recurrence when inherited visual context is treated as the task's own setting.
b.response: Suggested repair: suppress only verified matching metadata and display every differing deadline or recurrence beside the task; Details always retains exact values.
b.scoreReason: Removes repeated facts at their source while retaining exceptions and full metadata; exact matching rules remain a meaningful implementation risk.

revisedWinner.mechanism: Print labeled shared context once per matching block; show all differing deadlines, recurrence and scope, and describe inherited context without changing task settings.
revisedWinner.visible: Exact period, inclusion scope, titles/counts, completion and every meaningful context exception.
revisedWinner.disclosed: Context exposes existing period navigation, inclusion and duration; task Details retains full original metadata and editors; Options preserves existing menus.
revisedWinner.access: 44px contextual buttons, semantic exception text, explicit inherited-context descriptions, visible keyboard focus and wrapping at 320px.

a.attack: Repeated global and local scope sentences can consume the entire initial viewport before any cleaning task appears on a 320px phone.
a.response: Suggested repair: use one global sentence and repeat short local captions only when inclusion differs, keeping a named scope-change control adjacent.
a.scoreReason: Explicit language is useful when interrupted, but wording repetition and a management surface add height without fully governing metadata redundancy.

b.attack: A provenance caption can suggest that all visible monthly work belongs to the selected month even when accumulated weekly tasks come from earlier periods.
b.response: Suggested repair: label captions as view context rather than task history and preserve differing task dates or recurrence beside the specific item.
b.scoreReason: Block-level provenance handles redundancy and exception scope coherently; slightly more specific about mixed-cycle context than a global sentence alone.

revisedWinner.mechanism: Use one provenance caption per truly matching block, explicitly identifying view context; retain direct local disclosure for differing scope and recurrence.
revisedWinner.visible: Exact selected period, active scope, counts, completion and differing task frequency or date context.
revisedWinner.disclosed: Provenance exposes navigator, inclusion and diagnostic; task Details retains complete metadata and editors; existing Options stays locally available.
revisedWinner.access: 44px captions that act as buttons, full contextual names, keyboard disclosure and focus return; wrap short local captions at 320px.

a.attack: A wide desktop row can place inspection far from the task title, causing the wrong task's Details to be opened during rapid completion.
a.response: Suggested repair: bound task-row content width, label inspection by task identity, and keep completion and inspection as separate nonoverlapping targets.
a.scoreReason: Strong separation of finishing and inspecting supports the core workflow, with concrete safeguards against propagation and accidental edits.

b.attack: A long list with several open section action shelves puts repeated controls before tasks and makes collapse look like a management command.
b.response: Suggested repair: keep collapse independent, default shelves closed and expose a single named local Actions opener with persistent scope caption.
b.scoreReason: Local command scope is clear, but shelf duplication increases list height and does less to protect rapid task completion.

revisedWinner.mechanism: Keep leading completion and trailing inspection lanes within bounded row width; use object-specific inspection labels and preserve current period, inclusion and original Start eligibility.
revisedWinner.visible: Completion, titles, exact period, active scope and original Start action.
revisedWinner.disclosed: Task Details preserves metadata; scoped Inspection retains estimates, diagnostics and inclusion; separate Options retains unchanged menus.
revisedWinner.access: 44px nonoverlapping completion/inspection targets, descriptive names, stable keyboard order, narrow-row wrapping and stopped event propagation.

a.attack: A nested task at 320px cannot accommodate completion, title, due exception and a trailing information lane without compressing text or adding repeated controls.
a.response: Suggested repair: stack inspection below narrow rows while keeping the completion target and title together, with task-specific inspection names.
a.scoreReason: Clear action separation, but repeating information buttons and a rigid lane pattern compete with deeply nested content.

b.attack: Resizing while a scope menu is open can orphan its opener if the responsive layout replaces the trigger with a different compact component.
b.response: Suggested repair: change layout using CSS wrapping while preserving the trigger node, expanded state and focus relationship; measure long labels rather than assuming device width.
b.scoreReason: Addresses real content pressure and focus stability across all disclosure surfaces without imposing a new control pattern.

revisedWinner.mechanism: Wrap by available content width using stable trigger nodes; adapt spacing and placement without replacing focused controls, open-panel launchers or their state.
revisedWinner.visible: Title/completion, exact period, inclusion scope, counts and meaningful deadline exceptions.
revisedWinner.disclosed: Details retains every metadata action; header and section summaries expose estimates and breakdown; diagnostics, inclusion and original menus remain reachable.
revisedWinner.access: 44px nonoverlapping controls, stable DOM focus relationships, scoped labels, keyboard disclosure and 320px wrapping with reduced motion.

a.attack: Opening several full-width command stacks in a monthly list places dozens of 44px rows between tasks, weakening comparison and completion scanning.
a.response: Suggested repair: keep metadata initially collapsed and use independent named local openers; measure expanded heights and keep close controls easy to reach.
a.scoreReason: Reliable narrow-screen geometry, but blanket single-column commands are height-intensive and can overemphasize secondary settings.

b.attack: A summary drawer called only Resumen loses object scope when opened from two similarly named sections and adds an extra step to duration planning.
b.response: Suggested repair: label both opener and drawer with object identity, retain exact period/inclusion outside, and preview a relevant estimate beside the opener.
b.scoreReason: Predictable named inspection groups reduce competing surfaces while preserving distinct action menus and an estimate preview for planning.

revisedWinner.mechanism: Keep named summary drawers scoped by object; display exact period and inclusion beside their openers and a relevant compact estimate preview without duplicating management menus.
revisedWinner.visible: Title, selected period, inclusion scope, completion and explicitly scoped Resumen/Detalles openers.
revisedWinner.disclosed: Summary groups accumulated scope, estimates and diagnostics; task Details retains every editor and link; list and section menus stay separately named.
revisedWinner.access: 44px semantic openers, labeled dialogs, keyboard focus trapping where modal, reliable focus return and readable wrapping at 320px.

a.attack: Repeating context above every matching section can push the first actual task below the fold and make short lists feel like instructions.
a.response: Suggested repair: use one global context line and repeat section captions only for actual differences, preserving exceptional dates beside tasks.
a.scoreReason: One-column context establishes scope cleanly and handles narrow labels with fewer correctness assumptions than suppressing task dates broadly.

b.attack: A task due on the last day of a selected month may look redundant with month context despite its precise deadline being important for planning.
b.response: Suggested repair: define redundancy conservatively; keep precise deadlines unless truly equivalent, and expose original date editors through Details rather than a detached date inventory.
b.scoreReason: Useful deadline exception principle, but date equivalence and a dedicated shelf add correctness and navigation risk while addressing only one metadata family.

revisedWinner.mechanism: Place a wrapping global context line before the task list in one column; repeat local captions only for real differences and retain meaningful deadlines next to their tasks.
revisedWinner.visible: Exact period, inclusion scope, title/completion, counts and due exceptions.
revisedWinner.disclosed: Full-width Details retains metadata actions and breakdowns; separate Options and inclusion controls preserve original commands and diagnostic routes.
revisedWinner.access: 44px nonoverlapping controls, explicit local names, readable long Spanish captions, keyboard disclosure and focus return at 320px.

a.attack: A returning user's monthly list can accumulate a checkpoint, a period navigator and a Start confirmation sentence that repeat the same context three times.
a.response: Suggested repair: make the checkpoint the single context entry and repeat local checkpoints only for actual differences, preserving original Start eligibility.
a.scoreReason: Strong temporal safeguards for returning users, but introducing a checkpoint adds a contextual control to every relevant scope.

b.attack: If resting Details controls have inadequate contrast, keyboard-only emphasis can improve focus while touch users still cannot discover them.
b.response: Suggested repair: give all resting controls sufficient text contrast and visible labels; focus changes emphasis only, never availability or layout.
b.scoreReason: Stable visible controls reduce interaction surprise and preserve touch access; a broad hierarchy improvement with limited extra structural cost.

revisedWinner.mechanism: Keep labeled controls fixed with adequate resting contrast; emphasize the focused containing row without revealing new commands or shifting layout.
revisedWinner.visible: Completion, title, exact period, inclusion scope and visible Details/Options controls.
revisedWinner.disclosed: Expanded summaries retain dense facts and original metadata actions; focused rows gain restrained contrast while all routes remain discoverable at rest.
revisedWinner.access: 44px semantic targets, visible keyboard focus, adequate resting contrast for touch, stable control positions and reduced motion.

a.attack: Context opens a read-only summary that then routes to controls; changing a simple scope switch requires inspection and a second navigation decision.
a.response: Suggested repair: put existing controls beside their corresponding values inside the first summary, avoiding additional nested routing while keeping opening nonmutating.
a.scoreReason: Safe inspection and preserved routes, but broad summary navigation adds friction and still needs separate rules for duplicated status information.

b.attack: A count-first sentence that says own work is complete may misleadingly suggest all visible work is complete when accumulated tasks remain pending.
b.response: Suggested repair: explicitly distinguish own completion from included pending work and derive the sentence from existing status data, retaining exact period and scope.
b.scoreReason: Precisely removes redundant progress signals while preserving diagnostic access and critical completion distinctions; straightforward to verify against known status states.

revisedWinner.mechanism: Replace duplicated progress indicators with one count-first status sentence that distinguishes own completion from included pending work using unchanged status calculations.
revisedWinner.visible: Exact selected period, active inclusion scope, meaningful count sentence, task completion and relevant deadlines.
revisedWinner.disclosed: The semantic status control opens the existing diagnostic; secondary disclosure preserves duration, inclusion and all task metadata; original menus stay separately scoped.
revisedWinner.access: 44px status button, complete accessible name, wrapping count text, stable focus and keyboard access without duplicate spoken progress.

a.attack: Opening local inspectors across five nested sections can obscure the outline and invalidate virtualized row heights if each inspector is treated as decoration.
a.response: Suggested repair: default inspectors closed, measure expansion, keep section collapse independent, and provide only one original menu route per scope.
a.scoreReason: Keeps supporting context attached to the correct node while preserving original menu routes; manageable expansion cost with explicit measurement.

b.attack: Duration tiers can dominate a list containing an urgent unpaid bill with no duration, making a five-minute optional task seem more actionable.
b.response: Suggested repair: retain equally legible urgency, distinguish unknown estimates from zero, and limit duration emphasis to contexts where timing is relevant.
b.scoreReason: Preserves order and estimate routes but can prioritize one metadata type over deadlines and does less to reduce broader clutter.

revisedWinner.mechanism: Use an outline with closed local inline inspectors before section tasks; preserve independent collapse, measure expanded heights and avoid duplicate section menu routes.
revisedWinner.visible: Headings/counts, exact period, active inclusion scope, title/completion and named Details openers.
revisedWinner.disclosed: Local inspectors retain estimates, accumulated inclusion and the existing section Options; task Details retains metadata and links; global menu stays visible.
revisedWinner.access: 44px semantic controls, independent disclosure and collapse, visible focus, measured virtualized expansion and readable nesting at 320px.

a.attack: Native Details inside a clickable section header can toggle both metadata and section collapse when its summary click bubbles to the parent handler.
a.response: Suggested repair: place disclosure outside clickable header regions or stop its action propagation, preserve separate collapse controls and remeasure expanded rows.
a.scoreReason: Predictable native disclosure supports text reflow and distinct scopes, with concrete event and virtualization safeguards.

b.attack: A sticky active section can cover focused task controls at high zoom, especially when global navigation also remains fixed above it.
b.response: Suggested repair: allow only one sticky section depth, bound header height and set focus scroll margins; disable sticky behavior when the available viewport cannot fit it safely.
b.scoreReason: Reachable section context is valuable, but sticky geometry adds viewport and focus-occlusion risk without directly simplifying initial metadata density.

revisedWinner.mechanism: Use native Details groups with scope-specific names outside clickable collapse regions; remeasure expanded rows and preserve independent section collapse and unchanged action callbacks.
revisedWinner.visible: Titles, exact period, active scope, completion and named disclosure summaries.
revisedWinner.disclosed: Opened groups retain inclusion, duration, diagnostics and every metadata editor/link; existing menus retain their original subjects and callbacks.
revisedWinner.access: 44px native summaries, isolated events, visible keyboard focus, resilient text reflow and measured virtualized heights at zoom and 320px.
